newsitem.title: UK: POWELL DUFFRYN SELLS UK, S.AFRICA TERMINALS.
newsitem.headline: POWELL DUFFRYN SELLS UK, S.AFRICA TERMINALS.

text.p: Powell Duffryn Plc said it had entered into conditional agreements to sell its UK and South African terminals businesses to Koninklijke Van Ommeren of Rotterdam for 16.5 million stg in cash.
In a statement, the company added that it was writing down the book value of its three terminals in the U.S. by 15 million stg "to what is now indicated to be their realisable value."
The company said Van Ommeren had bought the leaseholds of its terminals at Durban, South Africa, along with Ipswich, Barry and Purfleet in Britain.
Van Ommeren also has a two-year option to buy the freehold property and plant at Purfleet at pre-determined prices or Powell Duffryn will sell the site.

Powell Duffryn will write off the Purfleet tankage at a book cost of 4.3 million stg and said the 2.3 million stg book value of the land was just below both the option price and estimated net realisable value.
The exceptional pre-tax gain resulting will be around 3.5 million stg and surplus attributable after tax and the South African minority interest will be just under two million stg.
Powell Duffryn said the U.S. terminals had yet to be sold and the write-down would also be treated as an exceptional item in results for the six months ending September 30. -- London
